precedence_rules: Major Accident Hazard overrides everything. Any credible loss-of-containment, well-control, or hazardous-area-integrity content takes the MAH label, even if an energy source is also named.

A named energy overrides Safety Systems. "Guard removed from grinder" is Mechanical -- the energy the barrier controls. Safety Systems applies only when the barrier/system itself is the subject and no specific energy dominates ("extinguisher blocked").
Among competing energies, the most severe credible outcome wins. A dropped object from height during lifting is Gravity rather than Motion.
Personal exposure vs. environmental harm. Chemical contact with people is Chemical; a release to the environment is Environment. Weather, sea state, ice, and lighting conditions are Environment.
Ergonomic/manual-handling strain is Other Hazard; body position in the line of fire of moving equipment is Motion.
Behaviour is never the label. Classify what the person is exposed to; the Human Factors dimension owns the behavioural driver.
Positive observations receive the hazard they successfully controlled ("good barriers around the lifting area" is Motion). Pure praise with no hazard content is N/A.

labels.label: Gravity
labels.keyword_triggers: dropped object, working at height, scaffold, ladder, handrail, harness, trip hazard, grating, hole cover, unsecured at height, slip
labels.guidance: Anything falling or a person falling, including same-level slips and trips. Not for loads being lifted or swinging (Motion) unless the drop itself is the stated concern.

labels.label: Motion
labels.keyword_triggers: line of fire, reversing, forklift, crane in operation, swinging load, moving equipment, pedestrian route, exclusion zone, projectile
labels.guidance: Things or people in motion; struck-by and caught-between. Not stored machine energy (Mechanical) and not objects falling under gravity (Gravity).

labels.label: Mechanical
labels.keyword_triggers: rotating, pinch point, guard missing, caught in, wire under tension, grinder, moving parts, stored energy, machinery isolation
labels.guidance: Machine energy and stored mechanical energy. A removed or missing guard classifies here, not Safety Systems.

labels.label: Electrical
labels.keyword_triggers: cable damaged, live, arc flash, socket, junction box open, lockout tagout, earthing, exposed wiring
labels.guidance: Shock, arc, and electrical isolation failures. A battery acid splash is Chemical.

labels.label: Pressure
labels.keyword_triggers: hose, whip check, pressurised, bleed down, hydraulic leak, cylinder, relief valve, pressure test
labels.guidance: Stored or released pressure at the working level. A falling cylinder is Gravity; process-scale containment loss is Major Accident Hazard.

labels.label: Temperature
labels.keyword_triggers: hot surface, steam, burn, scald, heat stress, insulation missing, cryogenic, hot work
labels.guidance: Thermal contact and thermal stress, hot or cold. Ambient weather cold and ice underfoot are Environment; ignition/flammable-atmosphere concerns escalate to Chemical or MAH.

labels.label: Chemical
labels.keyword_triggers: chemical, fumes, H2S, gas test, COSHH, SDS, corrosive, solvent, confined space atmosphere, splash
labels.guidance: Harmful substances/atmospheres threatening people. A release to sea or deck drain is Environment; process loss of containment is MAH.

labels.label: Biological
labels.keyword_triggers: hygiene, food, galley, mould, sewage, potable water, legionella, bites, sharps
labels.guidance: Biological agents and hygiene, including food safety and water quality.

labels.label: Radiation
labels.keyword_triggers: radiography, NORM, UV, welding flash, laser, antenna, radar, dosimeter, radiation barrier
labels.guidance: Ionising and non-ionising radiation sources and controls.

labels.label: Sound
labels.keyword_triggers: noise, hearing protection, ear defenders, ear plugs, decibel, noise zone
labels.guidance: Noise as a hearing risk. Noise as a distraction affecting performance belongs to Human Factors.

labels.label: Safety Systems
labels.keyword_triggers: fire extinguisher, eyewash, alarm inhibited, interlock bypassed, escape route blocked, fire door, muster point, signage missing, lifeboat, LSA, emergency lighting, no permit
labels.guidance: The barrier/emergency system itself is the subject. If the barrier protects against one clear energy (machine guard, fall arrest), classify that energy instead.

labels.label: Environment
labels.keyword_triggers: weather, wind limits, sea state, ice, poor lighting, visibility, spill to sea, deck drain, waste segregation, overboard
labels.guidance: Natural conditions risking people, and harm to the environment. Personal chemical contact is Chemical.

labels.label: Major Accident Hazard
labels.keyword_triggers: loss of containment, hydrocarbon leak, gas release, gas alarm, well control, flange leak, Ex equipment, hazardous area, structural integrity
labels.guidance: Overrides every other label when credible process-safety content is present, even if an energy is also named.

labels.label: Other Hazard
labels.keyword_triggers: manual handling, awkward lifting, posture, repetitive strain, security, unauthorised access
labels.guidance: A real hazard fitting none of the above. Keep small (target under ~3% of classified observations); a recurring theme should be flagged for the taxonomy owner to consider promoting to its own label.

labels.label: N/A - No Hazard Identified
labels.keyword_triggers: good job, thanks, well done, keep it up, no detail
labels.guidance: No identifiable hazard in the text. A positive card naming a controlled hazard takes that hazard's label, not N/A.

precedence_rules: Intent first. Deliberate deviation or deliberate good practice is Risk-Taking & Compliance Behaviour; unintended failure is Human Error.
Stated cause beats described act. When the text names why the act happened, classify the cause: "didn't isolate because the procedure is unclear" is Procedures & Documentation, not Human Error.
The most specific factor evidenced in the text wins; do not infer factors that are not written.
Performance shaper, not energy. Workplace and equipment content is classified here only as an influence on performance; the energy threat itself belongs to the Hazard dimension.
Fatigue and fitness-for-duty content in any form (roster, rest, alertness, heat exhaustion as a state) goes to Fatigue & Fitness for Duty.
Positive observations receive the factor demonstrated (a well-led toolbox talk is Leadership & Supervision). Pure praise with no factor content is N/A.

labels.label: Organisational Systems & Culture
labels.keyword_triggers: manning, roster system, management of change, permit system, always done this way, client pressure, waiting on parts
labels.guidance: Systems, resourcing, culture, and external pressure. Procedure content goes to Procedures & Documentation.

labels.label: Procedures & Documentation
labels.keyword_triggers: no procedure, out of date, doesn't match the plant, checklist missing, conflicting instructions, drawing wrong
labels.guidance: The written basis of work is missing, wrong, or unusable -- whether absent or impractical.

labels.label: Leadership & Supervision
labels.keyword_triggers: supervisor, toolbox talk, unsupervised, condoned, led by example, failed to enforce, leadership visit
labels.guidance: Line leadership quality, negative or positive.

labels.label: Communication & Handover
labels.keyword_triggers: handover, pre-job brief, radio, miscommunication, not informed, wrong information, language barrier
labels.guidance: Safety-critical information passing between people, shifts, crews, or vessel and shore.

labels.label: Training, Competence & Experience
labels.keyword_triggers: training, competence, unfamiliar, inexperienced, new to task, certification, induction, mentoring
labels.guidance: Knowledge, skills, and experience -- gaps or demonstrated strengths.

labels.label: Planning, Workload & Time Pressure
labels.keyword_triggers: rushed, time pressure, workload, poor plan, no plan, SIMOPS, conflicting jobs, awkward sequence
labels.guidance: How the job is planned and loaded. Roster-driven tiredness goes to Fatigue & Fitness for Duty.

labels.label: Equipment, Tools & Workplace Design
labels.keyword_triggers: wrong tool, defective, improvised, not available, poor design, confusing display, poor lighting, cramped access
labels.guidance: Tools, interfaces, and designed conditions as performance shapers. The energy threat itself belongs to the Hazard dimension.

labels.label: Fatigue & Fitness for Duty
labels.keyword_triggers: tired, fatigue, long shift, back-to-back, night shift, no rest, alertness, not fit for duty
labels.guidance: The person's physical or mental state relative to the task, from any cause.

labels.label: Human Error
labels.keyword_triggers: forgot, missed a step, misread, misjudged, accidentally, overlooked, didn't notice
labels.guidance: Unintentional failure. If the text states why it happened, classify the stated cause instead.

labels.label: Risk-Taking & Compliance Behaviour
labels.keyword_triggers: shortcut, didn't follow procedure, chose not to, PPE not worn, complacency, took a risk, intervened, stopped the job
labels.guidance: Deliberate deviation -- or deliberate good practice such as intervening and stopping the job.

labels.label: N/A
labels.keyword_triggers: good job, thanks, well done, no detail
labels.guidance: No human-factor content. A positive card demonstrating a factor takes that factor's label.

design_principles: Keywords suggest, they do not decide -- the definitions and precedence rules govern, and the AI should reason from context, not just string-match.
One primary label per dimension per card, always. Never return multiple labels for one dimension.

Behaviour/intent is never a Hazard label -- it always belongs to Human Factors. Conversely, workplace/equipment 'performance shaper' content is never a Hazard label -- the energy threat itself is Hazard, the influence on performance is Human Factors (Equipment, Tools & Workplace Design).
